text:
Ashley: Heads-up — enabled an nsys trace on the canary serving pool for ~30m and saw a few 99.9th tail spikes (90-200ms) that only appear while the trace is attached. baseline p99 is ~18ms so this looks like probe attenuation.
Mike: Can you paste the exact command you used? was it sampling mode or full capture? :eyes:
Ashley: ran this on the canary node: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/serving_probe --sample=cpu` and then collected the .nsys-rep. I also had `--capture-range=nvtx` toggled to limit capture window. overall avg overhead looked small but those spikes aligned with trace start/stop boundaries.
Jun: If you're toggling capture windows that often you'll hit scheduler jitter. nsys isn't free — even metadata + file flush can cause stalls. Did you collect results with `--stats`?
Ashley: yes, `--stats` showed +1.4% token throughput cost overall, but the scatter shows a few outliers. attaching the small excerpt:
```
EVENT, START_MS, DURATION_MS
ForwardKernelA, 123456.12, 0.98
KernelSync, 123456.35, 180.12  # these are the spikes when probe active
ForwardKernelB, 123456.60, 1.03
```
Priya: Two things: 1) prefer using periodic sampling (perf/periodic nsys sampling) instead of full timeline capture for prod. 2) run the tracer on a replica with headroom and redirect a small fraction of production traffic there.
Omar: +1. We built a small guardrail in runtime: `probe_fraction: 0.005` (0.5%) and `probe_mode: sampling` so only very small subset gets probed. That avoided measurable tail effects in canary.
Mike: Can you share what you measured when you moved to `probe_fraction: 0.005`? numbers? :thinking_face:
Ashley: after flipping to fraction and sampling-only: avg overhead <<1% and the 99.9th went back to ~20ms. No visible kernel stalls. We still see small I/O bumps when the replay writer rolls files every 5m.
Jun: Another low-impact option: attach ftrace/perf to the process (user-space sampling) and correlate with lightweight GPU metrics (NVML counters). That gives kernel hotspots without full context capture and doesn't trigger kernel timeline writes.
Priya: Also consider a SAFE_PROBE mode:
```
{
  "probe_mode": "sampling",
  "probe_fraction": 0.005,
  "max_concurrent_probes": 1,
  "attach_on_low_load_only": true
}
```
Omar: We added a circuit: if p95 latency for the probed replica increases by >5% during probe window, disable probes for 1h automatically. that avoided noisy experiments a few times.
Mike: For benchmarking, try `nvprof --metrics` on an offline copy of the model workload. nvprof can be lower-impact for per-kernel counters (but not full timelines). Also try `nsys --sample=periodic` rather than full trace.
Ashley: filing a short runbook note in #eng-runtime about safe_probe options and the rollout plan. I'll attach sample nsys flags we vetted.
ops-bot: deploy canary/probe-config updated by Ashley — 1954315600 — success :white_check_mark:
Jun: TL;DR: avoid full-perf capture in prod. prefer sampling, tiny probe_fraction, separate probe replicas, auto-circuit breakers, and prefer perf+NVML for hotspot IDs when possible. :thumbsup:
Priya: Added to runbook: "If any p99 spike >2x during probe, abort and revert config" — we can tune the threshold after more canary runs.
Ashley: thanks all — will iterate on thresholds and add a simple dashboard to show probe overhead for each replica.
